record.original_question: How to decide if eigenvalues of norm 1 may be allowed in the result stated just above? 2. Complexity issues In the literature, with a word several notions of complexity can be associated, the most famous one being certainly the factor complexity: given a word w, this complexity measures the number pw (n) of different factors of length n occuring in w. The famous characterization of Morse-Hedlund for ultimately periodic words led to introduce the infinite Surmian words whose complexity is pw (n) = n + 1, the best known example of them being certainly the famous Fibonacci word.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $h:A^*\to A^*$ be a morphism. The incidence matrix of $h$ is the $|A|\times|A|$ matrix $M_h$ whose entry $(M_h)_{a,b}$ counts the number of occurrences of the letter $a$ in the image $h(b)$. The morphism $h$ is called primitive if some power $M_h^k$ has all entries strictly positive. For a letter $a\in A$ such that $h(a)$ begins with $a$ and $|h^n(a)|\to\infty$, write $h^{\omega}(a)$ for the (right) infinite fixed point of $h$ obtained as the limit of $h^n(a)$.

Two finite words $u,v\in A^*$ are called abelian-equivalent, written $u\sim_{\mathrm{ab}} v$, if for every letter $c\in A$ the number of occurrences of $c$ in $u$ equals that in $v$. A template over $A$ is a tuple $t=(p,e,v_0,\dots,v_k)$ where $p,e\in A^*$ and each $v_i\in\mathbb{Z}^{|A|}$; a finite word $w$ is said to realize the template $t$ if $w$ admits a factorization $w = p\, u_1\, u_2\cdots u_k\, e$ such that for each $i$, the Parikh vector of $u_{i+1}$ minus the Parikh vector of $u_i$ equals $v_i$ (so that templates uniformly encode the standard notions of abelian $k$-th powers and their generalizations). One says that $h^{\omega}(a)$ realizes the template $t$ if some factor of $h^{\omega}(a)$ realizes $t$.

It is known that there is an algorithm which, given a primitive morphism $h$ whose incidence matrix $M_h$ has no eigenvalue of (complex) absolute value equal to $1$, a letter $a$ as above, and any template $t$, decides whether $h^{\omega}(a)$ realizes $t$.

Problem. Determine whether this decidability result extends to the case where $M_h$ is allowed to have eigenvalues of absolute value $1$: that is, give an algorithm which, on input an arbitrary primitive morphism $h$ (with no restriction on the spectrum of $M_h$), an admissible letter $a$, and a template $t$, decides whether $h^{\omega}(a)$ realizes $t$, or else show that no such algorithm exists.
artifact.category_tag: Combinatorics on words / abelian repetitions in morphic sequences
artifact.status_search_result: The decidability theorem of Rao and Rosenfeld (2015/2017) requires the incidence matrix of the primitive morphism to have no eigenvalue of modulus 1; the question of whether eigenvalues of norm 1 may be allowed is posed as an open question. Available sources (Rosenfeld's PhD thesis and follow-up work) discuss "small eigenvalues" but do not announce a resolution of the norm-1 case, so the current status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of Abelian Repetitions in Words (M. Rosenfeld, PhD thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Sections including 'Deciding Whether a Morphic Word is Abelian k-th Power Free' and 'Small eigenvalues and morphic words' treat decidability under spectral conditions on the incidence matrix.
status_evidence.claim: Rosenfeld's thesis develops the decidability result for primitive morphisms under eigenvalue restrictions, leaving the eigenvalue-of-norm-1 case as a non-trivial situation.

status_evidence.title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures (arXiv:1705.04055)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems from the WORDS meetings, including the question of whether eigenvalues of norm 1 may be allowed in the Rao–Rosenfeld decidability result on templates in fixed points of primitive morphisms.
status_evidence.claim: The question is recorded as an open problem in a compilation of open problems from the WORDS conference series.
